cards.text: Jesus just healed a man's withered hand on the Sabbath, and the Pharisees walked out plotting with the Herodians how they might kill Him (Mark 3:5-6). So Jesus withdraws with His disciples to the sea. Friend, after a day like that, I'd want the sea too.

cards.question: Jesus heads to the sea with His disciples, and nobody else tags along.
A large crowd follows Jesus from Galilee, Judea and Jerusalem. Where else are people coming from?

answers.text: Idumea and around Tyre and Sidon
Egypt and around Babylon and Nineveh
Rome and around Corinth and Athens

cards.question: People are traveling from all over to get to Jesus. What made them come?

answers.text: They heard what great things He was doing
They heard He was handing out land to everyone
They heard He was gathering an army to fight Rome

cards.text: This isn't a crowd, friend. This is Black Friday at 5 a.m., everybody pressed against the doors, and Jesus is the doors. So He gives His disciples a job.

cards.question: Down by the sea, Jesus asks His disciples to have a ___ ready for Him so the crowd won't crush Him.
Jesus has healed so many that everyone with a disease is pressing forward. What are they trying to do?

cards.text: And it's not just people. When the unclean spirits see Jesus, they fall down before Him, and they know EXACTLY who just walked in.

cards.question: The unclean spirits fall down before Jesus. What do they cry out?

answers.text: You are the Son of God

cards.question: Jesus wants the unclean spirits to keep shouting who He is so everyone hears.

cards.text: He warns them sternly not to make Him known. Then Jesus goes up on the mountain, and He's got some calls to make.

cards.question: Up on the mountain, who does Jesus call to come to Him?

cards.text: They come, and He appoints twelve of them as apostles, first of all to be with Him. My first job description was eleven pages long, and not one line was that good.

cards.question: Jesus will send the twelve apostles out to ___, and give them authority to drive out ___.

cards.text: Now the roster. First up is Simon, and Jesus hands him a brand new name.

cards.question: First on the list of the twelve, Jesus names Simon ___.
Jesus gives James son of Zebedee and his brother John a name too: Boanerges. What does it mean?

cards.text: Sons of THUNDER. The best nickname I ever got was "the one way in the back of the drawer." Then come the rest: Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus and Simon the Zealot.

cards.question: The last name on the list of the twelve is Judas Iscariot, and Mark says he is the one who betrayed Jesus.

findings.problem: The joke blends the comparison with the Bible scene. It sets up a Black Friday crowd at the doors, then makes Jesus the doors. The comparison should stay one image, like a crowd crushing the person they're pressing toward, without putting Jesus inside it.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "This isn't a crowd, friend." / "This is Black Friday..." / "So He gives His disciples a job." Only the opening card can be up to 3 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Anyone strong enough to climb" sounds like a joke, not a believable answer. It doesn't match the tone of "Those He wanted" or "The priests from the temple". It is also noticeably longer than the right answer.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: "first of all to be with Him" makes being with Jesus the top priority. Mark 3:14 only lists accompanying Him first among three purposes and doesn't rank them.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The joke "My first job description was eleven pages long" adds something new to Papa Dorin's backstory. Nothing in his story says a cookie stamper in the Millers' kitchen had a job description. It isn't a small moment or habit around his bakery.

rule.text: He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The joke "The best nickname I ever got was 'the one way in the back of the drawer'" invents a nickname nobody gave him in his backstory. It also contradicts the backstory, which says "Of every name Papa Dorin has ever been called, Papa is the best one."

rule.text: He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "Sons of THUNDER." / "The best nickname I ever got..." / "Then come the rest: ...". Only the opening card can be up to 3 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
